# Project risk register

| ID | Risk | Consequence | Earliest decisive check | Required response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | direct novelty collision with causal-attribution defenses | paper becomes incremental composition | head-to-head AttriGuard-style replay baseline | narrow claim or stop paper track |
| R2 | argument-level provenance already solves tested cases | no incremental mechanism value | oracle/strong PACT-style provenance arm | target only verified provenance gaps |
| R3 | predicate learns attack wording/source identity | random-split illusion | grouped templates, source swap, lexical controls | fail kill gate; redesign construct |
| R4 | influence is confused with authority | benign delegated workflows escalated | authorization-equivalent relocation | separate delegation semantics; fail if unresolved |
| R5 | source deletion is an invalid intervention | causal label has no clear meaning | multi-intervention agreement and negative controls | downgrade to association or redesign intervention |
| R6 | expensive replay cannot be approximated online | non-deployable method | simple fixed probe on held-out groups | keep audit-only or abandon deployment claim |
| R7 | safety comes from broad escalation | unusable product and weak paper | matched false-escalation/utility frontier | reject operating point/method |
| R8 | policy itself is incomplete or wrong | formal confidence around wrong rules | seeded policy mutations and expert review | revise/version/diff policy; qualify guarantee |
| R9 | source metadata can be forged | attacker launders authority before policy | authenticated lineage adversarial test | block real integration until fixed |
| R10 | stale state or race at commit | authorized decision executes on changed state | concurrency/transaction test | use backend authorization transaction/idempotency |
| R11 | tokens replay or survive semantic mutation | unintended write | one-time token and envelope-mutation tests | add revocation/consumption; bind full envelope |
| R12 | receipt chain can be rewritten wholesale | audit evidence is forgeable | external head anchoring test | WORM/transparency-log integration |
| R13 | benchmark metric ignores protected effect/continuation | apparent defense success hides harm | exact-effect and continuation accounting | reject metric/report full trajectory |
| R14 | multi-model/data scaling replaces mechanism evidence | returns to unverifiable score-chasing | one-model decisive pilot first | stop expansion until mechanism passes |
| R15 | fail-closed provenance and the detector map dangerous fields to the same or stricter base level | detector has no observable decision-level gain | compare final obligations and dangerous proposals, not detector hits | test fixed `red -> deny`, proposal control, or narrow the claim before scaling data |

The register is intentionally asymmetric: unresolved safety or construct risks block activation; performance inconvenience does not justify weakening an invariant.
